name: Rushmi Chakravarthi
bio:
Career Overview: Rushmi Chakravarthi is a retired Indian tennis player, renowned for holding the record for the most ITF titles by an Indian woman, retiring in 2017 after a prolific career.

Playing Style: Known for her consistent baseline game and endurance, she excelled on hard courts.

Career-High WTA Singles Ranking: #314 (October 31, 2005)
Career-High WTA Doubles Ranking: #208 (October 24, 2005)

Best Grand Slam Singles Performance: Reached the first round of Wimbledon qualifying in 2005.

Notable Achievements:
  • Won a record 11 ITF singles titles and 41 ITF doubles titles, totaling 52—the highest by an Indian woman.
  • Earned 4 medals at the 2006 Asian Games (team gold, doubles silver, mixed doubles bronze, singles bronze).
  • Won a bronze medal in doubles at the 2010 Commonwealth Games with Sania Mirza.

Other Highlights:
  • A Fed Cup stalwart for India from 2000–2012, with a win-loss record of 22–18.
  • Competed at the 2012 London Olympics in doubles with Sania Mirza, reaching the first round.
  • Mentored younger players post-retirement, contributing to Indian tennis development.

Rushmi’s prolific ITF career solidified her as a key figure in Indian tennis history. 🎾🇮🇳
